title: Paying Off Debt 'Wrong' Beats Perfect Math
hook: The mathematically optimal way to pay off debt has one fatal flaw — humans. And Harvard researchers found the 'wrong' method pays off 14% more debt.
angle: The debt avalanche (highest APR first) is mathematically superior but causes most people to quit due to slow visible progress. The debt snowball (smallest balance first) wins in real-world testing because emotional momentum outweighs interest savings.
audience: Anyone juggling multiple credit cards or loans who wants to pay off debt faster
key_numbers: 14% — more debt eliminated by snowball users vs avalanche users in research
24.99% — typical high-end credit card APR that avalanche targets first
$6,360 — average American credit card debt per person
$800–$1,200 — interest savings avalanche has over snowball on a typical balance
90 days — timeframe to find a 'quick win' balance to start your snowball
